# Remove-ZbxSla

## SYNOPSIS

Removes SLAs.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxSla [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixSlaRecord>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A service level agreement sets the uptime a set of services should reach in each reporting period, and reports what they reached. The Remove-ZbxSla cmdlet deletes the SLAs given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with sla.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete an SLA

```powershell
Remove-ZbxSla -InputObject 'Business hours SLA' -Confirm:$false
```

Deletes the SLA Business hours SLA. -Confirm:$false skips the prompt the command shows by default.

### Example 2: Preview deleting the SLAs a search finds

```powershell
Get-ZbxSla -Name 'Business*' | Remove-ZbxSla -WhatIf
```

Lists the SLAs whose names start with Business that the command would delete, and deletes nothing.
